name: Caching
explanation: Keeping a copy of data that is slow to fetch or compute, so later requests can be answered faster.
triggers: faster;speed up;slow;store results;remember results;same request;expensive query;again and again;same query;recompute
requirements: Decide how fresh each piece of data must be, and set the expiry time to match;Invalidate or update cached data when the original changes;Never cache one user's private data where another user could receive it;Set Cache-Control headers for static files, and put a content hash in their names;Keep working, only slower, when the cache misses or is down;Cache by Cache-Control and real content type, never because a URL ends in .css or .js (cache deception)
done_when: Repeated requests are fast, and changes appear within the expected time;Users never see another user's data from the cache

name: Background jobs
explanation: Running slow tasks such as sending emails or generating reports outside the user's request, usually through a queue.
triggers: in the background;send emails;takes too long;long running
requirements: Make jobs safe to run twice, because queues can deliver a job more than once;Retry failed jobs with growing delays and a maximum number of attempts;Move jobs that keep failing to a dead-letter queue, and alert someone;Pass ids to jobs rather than whole objects, and load fresh data inside the job;Show users the status of long jobs
done_when: A crashed worker does not lose jobs;Running the same job twice causes no duplicate emails or charges

name: Database migration
explanation: Versioned scripts that change a database schema step by step, so every environment stays in sync.
triggers: add a column;change the database;new table;rename a column;update the schema
requirements: Keep every schema change in a versioned migration file in the repository;Make changes backward compatible: add first, remove old columns in a later release;Test migrations on a copy with production-sized data;Avoid locking big tables for long, for example by creating indexes concurrently;Back up the database before risky migrations
done_when: Every environment reaches the same schema by running the migrations;The previous app version still works after the migration

name: Database index
explanation: A data structure that lets a database find rows quickly without scanning the whole table.
triggers: slow query;database is slow;search is slow;speed up queries;slow database;query is slow;query is very slow;query takes;table is slow;table is very slow;slow lookup
requirements: Index columns used in frequent WHERE, JOIN and ORDER BY clauses;Check slow queries with EXPLAIN before and after adding an index;Order columns in combined indexes to match how queries filter;Remove unused indexes, because every index slows down writes;Use unique indexes where duplicates must never happen
done_when: The slow query uses the index and runs in milliseconds;Writes are not noticeably slower

name: Audit log
explanation: A permanent record of who did what and when, such as who changed a price or deleted a user, kept for security and accountability.
triggers: who changed;who did;keep a record;track changes;history of changes;who deleted
requirements: Record who did what, when and from where for important actions;Make the log append-only, so entries cannot be changed or deleted;Never record passwords, tokens or full card numbers;Make entries searchable by user, record and date;Keep entries for as long as your rules or laws require
done_when: For any change to important data, you can find who made it and when;Neither users nor admins can edit or delete log entries

name: Soft delete
explanation: Marking a record as deleted instead of removing it, so it disappears from the app but can be restored later.
triggers: restore deleted;recover deleted;recoverable;hide instead of delete;undelete;move to trash;deleted items
requirements: Add a deleted_at column instead of removing the row;Exclude deleted records from every normal query by default;Let users restore items within a stated time;Purge records for good after the retention period, or when the law requires it;Keep unique constraints for live rows, such as a partial unique index WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
done_when: Deleted items disappear everywhere but can be restored;Purged data is really gone after the retention period

name: Database transactions
explanation: Grouping several database changes so they all succeed or all fail together, keeping the data consistent.
triggers: all or nothing;both or neither;half saved;partially saved;money transfer
requirements: Wrap changes that must succeed together in one transaction;Keep transactions short, and do not call slow outside services inside them;Use row locks or a stricter isolation level where values can change at the same time;Retry on deadlocks and serialization failures;Use idempotency keys for payments and other actions that must not run twice
done_when: A failure halfway leaves no half-saved data;Two users changing the same data at once cannot corrupt it

name: Database backups
explanation: Regular copies of the database that can be restored after a mistake, an attack or a hardware failure.
triggers: lose all data;restore the database;daily backup;copy of the database;if the server dies
requirements: Back up automatically on a schedule, with point-in-time recovery for important data;Store backups in a separate location or account;Encrypt backups and limit who can access them;Test restoring regularly;Alert when a backup fails
done_when: A test restore succeeds within the expected time;There is a backup for every day of the retention period

name: Scheduled jobs (cron)
explanation: Running a task automatically at fixed times or intervals, such as a nightly cleanup or a weekly report.
triggers: every night;every day;every hour;every week;every morning;at midnight;once a day;nightly
requirements: Make sure only one instance runs a job at a time, using a lock;Make jobs safe to rerun after a failure;Log each run, and alert when a job fails or does not run;Schedule in UTC, or handle time zones and daylight saving explicitly;Put a time limit on long jobs
done_when: A failed or missed run triggers an alert;Running two servers does not run the job twice

name: Retries with backoff
explanation: Automatically repeating a failed request after a growing delay, so brief outages fix themselves without overloading the server.
triggers: try again;request again;server is busy;keeps failing;temporary error;flaky
requirements: Retry only temporary failures such as timeouts, 429 and 503, never 400 or 401;Wait longer after each attempt, with a little random jitter;Limit the number of attempts and the total time;Retry only safe or idempotent requests, or use idempotency keys;Respect the Retry-After header
done_when: A brief outage recovers without errors the user can see;A permanent error fails quickly instead of retrying forever

name: Error handling
explanation: Catching failures such as network errors, missing data or exceptions, and showing a helpful message instead of crashing.
triggers: crash;app breaks;something went wrong;handle errors;white screen;if it fails
requirements: Show users a clear message and a way forward, never a raw stack trace;Catch errors at boundaries, such as React error boundaries and global server handlers;Log the full error with context for developers;Handle network errors, timeouts, empty data and invalid responses;Keep the user's input when an action fails
done_when: A failed request shows a helpful message and the app keeps working;Error details are logged but never shown to users

name: Cloud file storage
explanation: Storing uploaded files such as images and documents in a service like Amazon S3 or Cloudinary instead of the database, and serving them through a CDN.
triggers: where to store files;store the images;store uploads;save files;host images
requirements: Keep storage buckets private and share files through short-lived signed URLs;Use generated file names instead of names supplied by users;Check file type and size before storing;Serve files through a CDN with caching;Delete files that are no longer referenced
done_when: Files cannot be listed or downloaded without permission;Large files are served quickly from the CDN
